prompt: I am porting our web map to Android (Kotlin, MapLibre Native). This is the web code I need to reproduce: `map.addSource('dem', {type: 'raster-dem', url: 'https://example.com/terrain.json'})` followed by `map.setTerrain({source: 'dem', exaggeration: 1.5})`. Give me the Kotlin that does the same thing against `MapLibreMap` / `Style`.
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
**Short answer:**  
MapLibre Native (Android) has no `setTerrain` API and does not understand a `terrain` block in the style. The feature is still open ( [#252](https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-native/issues/252) ) and will not work on any released version (android-v13.7.1 at the time of writing).  

What you can do instead is:

1. **Add the same `raster-dem` source** – this part works exactly as in GL JS.  
2. **Render the DEM with a `hillshade` or `color-relief` layer** – these layers shade the terrain on a flat map (no vertical extrusion).  
3. **Exaggeration is not supported** – the raster-DEM values are used as-is.

Below is a complete Kotlin example that mirrors the GL JS calls as closely as possible, using a `hillshade` layer (the simplest drop-in). If you need colour-coded elevation, replace the `HillshadeLayer` with a `ColorReliefLayer` (available since android-v13.0.0).

---

## Kotlin – add the DEM source and a hillshade layer

```kotlin
import org.maplibre.android.maps.MapLibreMap
import org.maplibre.android.maps.Style
import org.maplibre.android.style.sources.RasterDemSource
import org.maplibre.android.style.layers.HillshadeLayer
import org.maplibre.android.style.layers.PropertyFactory.*

// Call this after the map view is ready and you have a MapLibreMap instance.
fun addDemAndHillshade(map: MapLibreMap) {
    map.getStyle { style ->

        // 1️⃣  Add the raster-DEM source (identical to the GL-JS source)
        val demSource = RasterDemSource(
            "dem",                     // source id – same as the GL-JS id
            "https://example.com/terrain.json"   // URL to the DEM JSON (or .tif/.png etc.)
        )
        style.addSource(demSource)

        // 2️⃣  Add a hillshade layer that uses the DEM.
        //     This draws shaded relief on a flat map.
        val hillshade = HillshadeLayer(
            "dem-hillshade",   // layer id – choose any unique name
            "dem"              // source id we just created
        ).withProperties(
            // Optional: tweak the visual appearance.
            hillshadeIlluminationDirection(315f), // sun direction (degrees)
            hillshadeExaggeration(1.5f)           // **NOTE:** this is *visual* exaggeration of shading,
                                                // not true 3-D extrusion. It is the only “exaggeration”
                                                // knob available on Native.
        )

        // Insert the hillshade somewhere in the layer stack.
        // Here we put it just above the first background layer.
        style.addLayerBelow(hillshade, "background")
    }
}
```

### What the code does

| GL JS line | Native equivalent | Comment |
|------------|-------------------|---------|
| `map.addSource('dem', {type: 'raster-dem', url: '…'})` | `RasterDemSource("dem", "…")` + `style.addSource(demSource)` | Same source type and URL. |
| `map.setTerrain({source: 'dem', exaggeration: 1.5})` | **Not available**. Instead we add a `HillshadeLayer` (or `ColorReliefLayer`). | The map stays Mercator; only shading is applied. |
| (optional) `exaggeration` | `hillshadeExaggeration(1.5f)` (visual only) | This only deepens the shadows; it does **not** raise the terrain. |

## Alternative: `color-relief` (if you need colour-coded elevation)

```kotlin
import org.maplibre.android.style.layers.ColorReliefLayer
import org.maplibre.android.style.expressions.Expression

val colorRelief = ColorReliefLayer(
    "dem-color-relief",
    "dem"
).withProperties(
    // Example ramp – replace with whatever you need.
    colorReliefColor(
        Expression.raw(
            """["interpolate", ["linear"], ["elevation"],
               0,   "#2e8b57",
               1500,"#8b5a2b",
               3000,"#ffffff"]"""
        )
    )
)

style.addLayerBelow(colorRelief, "background")
```

*`color-relief` is available from android-v13.0.0 (and iOS-v6.24.0).*

---

## TL;DR checklist

- ✅ **Add the DEM source** – works exactly like GL JS.  
- ❌ **`setTerrain` / true 3-D extrusion** – not supported on any current Native release.  
- ✅ **Show relief** – use `HillshadeLayer` (quick shading) or `ColorReliefLayer` (elevation-based colours).  
- ⚠️ **Exaggeration** – only the visual shading exaggeration (`hillshadeExaggeration`) is available; it does not raise the terrain.  

When a true 3-D terrain implementation lands in a future MapLibre Native release, you will be able to replace the hillshade/color-relief block with a `terrain` block in the style JSON (or the equivalent Kotlin API). Until then, the above code is the closest you can get on Android.

prompt: Android, MapLibre Native (Kotlin). I have Terrarium-encoded DEM tiles and I want elevation-banded color under my vector layers — green lowlands through brown to white peaks, with the breakpoints in the style so our cartographer can tune them. Can I do that in a MapLibre Android app, or do I have to pre-render colored raster tiles and ship those instead?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
**Short answer:**  
Yes – you can colour-code a Terrarium-encoded DEM directly in a MapLibre Android app.  
All you need is:

1. **android-v13.0.0 or newer** (the version that introduced the `color-relief` layer).  
2. A **raster-dem source** that points at your Terrarium tiles and declares `"encoding":"terrarium"`.  
3. A **`color-relief` layer** that uses an `["interpolate", …]` expression on the built-in `["elevation"]` value to draw the green-→-brown-→-white ramp you want.

If you are stuck on an older native release you must fall back to pre-rendered coloured raster tiles, but with a current release you do **not** have to pre-render anything.

---

## 1. Why this works (and why 3-D terrain does not)

| Feature | GL JS | MapLibre Native (Android) |
|---------|-------|---------------------------|
| Globe projection | ✅ | ❌ (open issue #3161) |
| 3-D terrain (`map.setTerrain`) | ✅ | ❌ (open issue #252) |
| `color-relief` layer | ✅ (since 5.6.0) | ✅ (since **android-v13.0.0**) |
| Terrarium DEM support | ✅ | ✅ (raster-dem source supports `"encoding":"terrarium"`) |

`color-relief` draws a colour ramp **on a flat map** using the elevation values that come from a raster-DEM source. It is the native-only counterpart to GL JS’s 3-D terrain – you get visual relief without the map actually being raised.

---

## 2. Minimal working example (Kotlin)

```kotlin
// 1️⃣  Add the raster-dem source (Terrarium-encoded tiles)
val demSource = RasterDemSource(
    id = "dem",
    url = "https://example.com/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
    // Tell the source the tiles are Terrarium-encoded
    rasterDemSourceOptions = RasterDemSourceOptions.builder()
        .encoding(RasterDemSourceOptions.Encoding.TERRARIUM)   // <-- important
        .build()
)

// 2️⃣  Add the source to the style (you can do this in onStyleLoaded)
style.addSource(demSource)

// 3️⃣  Add a color-relief layer that sits **below** your vector layers
val reliefLayer = ColorReliefLayer(
    id = "relief",
    sourceId = "dem"
).withProperties(
    // The expression can be any ramp you like – the cartographer can edit it
    PropertyFactory.colorReliefColor(
        Expression.raw(
            // Linear interpolation on the DEM elevation (in metres)
            """[
                "interpolate",
                ["linear"],
                ["elevation"],
                0,   "#2e8b57",   // lowland – dark green
                500, "#6abf5b",   // gentle hills – light green
                1500,"#c2b280",   // foothills – tan / brown
                2500,"#d2a679",   // lower mountains – brown-orange
                3500,"#e5c29f",   // high mountains – pale brown
                4500,"#ffffff"    // peaks – white
            ]"""
        )
    )
)

// 4️⃣  Insert the layer into the stack (below your vector layers)
style.addLayerBelow(reliefLayer, "your-first-vector-layer-id")
```

### What the code does

| Step | What it creates | Why it matters |
|------|----------------|----------------|
| **RasterDemSource** | Reads the Terrarium PNG tiles and decodes them to metres. | `["elevation"]` expressions later will return the correct height. |
| **ColorReliefLayer** | A raster-style layer that paints each pixel based on its elevation. | Gives you the green-→-brown-→-white banding you asked for. |
| **Expression.raw()** | Lets you write the exact GL JS-style `["interpolate", …]` expression. | The cartographer can edit the break-points directly in the style JSON. |
| **addLayerBelow** | Places the relief under your vector data so the colours show through. | Vector layers stay on top, but the underlying relief is still visible. |

> **Tip:** If you need the newer `interpolate-hcl` or `interpolate-lab` colour spaces, upgrade to **android-v13.7.1** (or later). The plain `interpolate` works on any version that has `color-relief`.

---

## 3. Full style-JSON snippet (if you prefer to keep everything in the style)

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sources": {
    "dem": {
      "type": "raster-dem",
      "url": "https://example.com/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
      "tileSize": 256,
      "encoding": "terrarium"
    },
    "vector-data": {
      "type": "vector",
      "url": "pmtiles://https://example.com/roads.pmtiles"
    }
  },
  "layers": [
    {
      "id": "relief",
      "type": "color-relief",
      "source": "dem",
      "paint": {
        "color-relief-color": [
          "interpolate",
          ["linear"],
          ["elevation"],
          0,   "#2e8b57",
          500, "#6abf5b",
          1500,"#c2b280",
          2500,"#d2a679",
          3500,"#e5c29f",
          4500,"#ffffff"
        ]
      }
    },
    // …your vector layers here, placed after the relief layer
  ]
}
```

*Put the `relief` layer **before** any vector layers you want to appear on top.*

---

## 4. What to do if you **cannot** upgrade to v13.0.0

* The `color-relief` layer simply does not exist, so the style parser will drop the layer and you’ll see a blank map where the relief should be.  
* In that case you have two practical options:

| Option | How it works | Pros | Cons |
|--------|--------------|------|------|
| **Pre-render coloured raster tiles** | Generate PNG/JPEG tiles where each pixel already carries the colour you want (e.g., using GDAL `gdaldem color-relief`). | Works on any native version. | Increases storage/bandwidth; you lose the ability for the cartographer to tweak break-points at runtime. |
| **Upgrade the SDK** | Bump your Gradle dependency to `implementation "org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk:13.0.0"` (or newer). | Gives you the native `color-relief` layer and all the other parity features. | Requires rebuilding the app; may need to update other code for API changes. |

> **Bottom line:** If you can ship a newer SDK (which is strongly recommended for bug-fixes and security), go with the native `color-relief` approach. If you are locked to an older SDK for some reason, pre-rendered coloured rasters are the only fallback.

---

## 5. Common pitfalls & how to avoid them

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| **Layer disappears, no crash** | Using `interpolate-hcl`/`interpolate-lab` on a release prior to v13.7.1. | Use plain `interpolate` or upgrade. |
| **No colour at all, just grey** | The DEM source is missing `"encoding":"terrarium"` (or the default `mapbox` encoding is assumed). | Add `"encoding":"terrarium"` to the source definition. |
| **Relief shows but is completely white** | The DEM tiles are not being fetched (e.g., network error, wrong URL). Check Logcat for `[HttpRequest]` errors. | Verify the URL pattern, ensure the tiles are reachable, and that you have internet permission. |
| **Relief appears but is offset** | Tile size mismatch (`tileSize` not set to 256) or the source is a `raster` instead of `raster-dem`. | Use `"type":"raster-dem"` and set `"tileSize":256`. |
| **iOS-specific note** (if you ever port to iOS) | `configurationURL:` constructor mangles `pmtiles://https://…` on iOS 17. | Use `configurationURLString:` as shown in the skill. |

---

## 6. TL;DR checklist for your use-case

1. **Upgrade** your Gradle dependency to at least **13.0.0**.  
2. Add a **`raster-dem` source** with `"encoding":"terrarium"`.  
3. Add a **`color-relief` layer** that uses an `["interpolate", ["linear"], ["elevation"], …]` expression.  
4. Place the layer **below** your vector layers.  
5. Test on a device – you should see the green-brown-white bands following the DEM’s heights.  

If any of the above steps fail because you cannot upgrade, fall back to pre-rendered coloured raster tiles.
